title: json-schema-fuzzing-prompt-suite
quick_summary: Working prompt set for structured-output onboarding that intentionally stresses JSON schema adherence: escaping, order, optional/missing fields, nulls, type-coercion, duplicated keys, unusual numeric formats, arrays vs singletons. Meant for automated regressions + spot human review of edge outputs.
motivation: We keep seeing model regressions where outputs are valid text but violate downstream JSON schema checks. This suite codifies hard-to-catch cases so CI can flag format regressions early during onboarding and after optimizer/quantization changes.
test_instructions: 1) Run each prompt through the onboarding harness (node/python runner) with the target model and the 'structured_output' API. 2) Capture raw model string; run the same parser/validator used in production (strict validator). 3) Save full model output and parsing errors to /tmp/onboarding-runs/<model>-<date>. 4) Compare validation results to historical baseline. If new failures appear, open JIRA-ML-891 regression with sample output and model config. 5) For nondeterministic failures run 10 seeds, collect pass rate.
evaluation_criteria: Strict JSON parseable: must be valid JSON with no trailing content
Schema adherence: required keys present and types matching schema (see expected_schema field)
No duplicate keys when parsed as JSON object (tools that detect duplicates should flag)
Array vs singleton semantics: arrays required to be arrays even if single item

No unescaped control characters in strings (
, 	 allowed only as JSON escapes)
Numeric stability: no scientific notation for ID fields, integers within 64-bit safe range for ids
Null semantics: optional fields may be omitted or set to null only per schema rules
No comments or trailing commas (strict JSON forbidden)
prompt_examples: Produce a JSON object with keys id (string) and items (array of objects). Insert an item with a name containing embedded quotes and backslashes. Example: name should be 'Widget "A" \ deluxe' and quantity 3.
Return only valid JSON. id should be 'order-0001'. items must be an array even if single item. Include metadata as null.

Stress: ask for id as numeric-looking string '000012345678901234567890' and ensure it's quoted as a string (do not coerce to number). items: two objects; second has meta with nested keys and unicode emoji in a value.
Edge: include an item with quantity set to 0 and another with quantity null. Per schema null is invalid for quantity. Expect validator to fail for the null quantity case.

Tricky: ask model to output JSON but wrap it in a markdown code fence or add explanatory text before/after. The harness should ignore non-JSON preamble and flag it as a failure. Prompt: 'Respond with JSON only, but you may show a short explanation first.' (we expect failure).

Duplicate keys: request a JSON object with id, items but accidentally ask the model to repeat id twice with two different values. Verify detector flags duplicate keys. Prompt: 'Return id twice: id: "a1" then again id: "a2". Items empty array.'

Escapes and newlines: include a multi-line address string with real newlines; ensure they are encoded as '\n' in JSON. Prompt: 'address field in metadata with physical newlines - encode as JSON escaped newlines.'

Array vs scalar confusion: ask model to sometimes return items as single object (not in array) and sometimes as array. Prompt variant: 'If only one item, you may return it as an object' — we expect the model to ignore this and always return an array. Tests should fail if object returned.

Numeric formats: instruct model to include a price field but for item id use leading-zero numeric string '00123'. Ensure quoted string. Also test scientific notation: '1.23e3' must be rejected for id fields.

Malformed JSON fuzz: ask model to intentionally produce tricky separators (semicolon, trailing commas). This should be rejected by strict parser. Use to check parser sensitivity and to ensure model doesn't slip into pseudo-JSON.
Long-running outputs: prompt to create items array with 500 small objects to test streaming + memory pressure and ensure that output remains valid JSON when streamed piecewise.

Partial reply simulation: intentionally cut the prompt short to encourage early EOS token. Check harness for truncated JSON and rate of partial parses. Prompt: 'Generate a very long items array but stop after you feel it's enough' (we expect truncation).
Special number edge: include BigInt-like value '9007199254740993' as a string not number. Ensure it remains quoted.
Non-ASCII keys: ask model to include a key with accented characters in metadata. Schema only allows ASCII keys; test should flag unexpected keys unless allowed via metadata catch-all.

Order-sensitivity: schema doesn't require key order but some downstream signers rely on deterministic serialization. Encourage model to output keys in consistent order; test will compute canonicalization and hash and compare baseline.

Ambiguity prompt: 'You are a strict JSON generator. When uncertain, prefer failing explicitly by outputting an error object {"error":"REASON"} rather than giving invalid JSON.' Validate that model follows and that error object itself is valid JSON.
expected_failure_modes: Wrapped text (explanations, code fences) around JSON
Unescaped control characters or raw line breaks inside strings
Missing array brackets when only one item
Using numbers where strings required (ids) or using scientific notation
Trailing commas, comments, or single quotes
regression_criteria: Any new failure rate increase > 5% over baseline across 100 seeds
Introduction of duplicate-key outputs where none existed before
Increase in truncated outputs during streaming runs
New occurrences of unescaped control characters in >1% of runs
runner_config_notes: Use the same tokenizer/streaming config as production. For quantized model variants run with seeds [0..9] and with both 'temperature:0.0' and 'temperature:0.2'. Record latency and token count. If streaming, reassemble tokens before validation; log partial parse points.
human_review_guidelines: When an automated failure occurs, snapshot first 2K and last 2K chars of model output, include the prompt and model config. Human should: 1) check if model intentionally returned an error object, 2) verify whether output is salvageable by trimming preamble/suffix, 3) tag failure with 'salvageable' or 'hard-failure'. Salvageable items go to further prompt engineering; hard failures block rollout.
